_doc:
Farhold's buildable things — BUILDING_EXPANSION.md §4c (decorative), §4d (manufacturing), §4e (defensive), plus the road, wall and waypoint pieces. Every entry is pure data: a footprint in metres, a material cost, a look recipe that js/build.js turns into boxes and cylinders, and the rules js/buildplan.js checks before it will let you put one down. NOTHING here knows about Three.js, so node --test can read the whole catalogue.

ON MATERIALS: the ids in `cost` are a CONTRACT, not an inventory. §1 (gathering) and §2 (refining) belong to another part of this expansion and will decide where `iron` or `plank` actually comes from; this file only says what a workbench costs. js/buildplan.js never reads a bag directly — it asks a `have(id)` callback the game supplies — so whichever store system wins, the catalogue does not change.

ON SLOPE: `slope` is the steepest ground a piece will accept under its corners, as rise over run. Most things want 0.18 (about a 1-in-5 bank), which almost nowhere on Farhold is, and that is deliberate: it is what sends the player to the smoothing tool in js/terraform.js first, exactly as §4.11 intends.

ON LIGHT: anything with a `light` block hands that block straight to js/light.js's source pool — the same pool the carried torch uses — so a lamp post genuinely lights the ground. §4c: 'they should be the first thing a player builds after walls, because Farhold's nights are dark and that is the point of them.'

No third-party IP: every name here is descriptive English.

rules._doc: grid: metres between snap points. snapDistance: how close a ghost has to be to an existing piece's edge before it jumps to it. refund: fraction of the cost the deconstruct tool gives back (§4.7 — 'building should not punish experimenting'). footingTolerance: how far a corner may sit off the ground before the piece counts as floating. claimRadius: metres from the claim stone.

decor.name: Decoration
decor._doc: §4c. None of them do anything, and that is the point.

light.name: Lighting
light._doc: §4c street lights. Real lights, in js/light.js's pool.

craft.name: Workshop
craft._doc: §3 benches. Each one unlocks a recipe family.

power.name: Power
power._doc: §8. Generation, storage and the poles between them.

store.name: Storage
store._doc: §8.1 pools: stores in reach of each other share everything.

defence.name: Defence
defence._doc: §4e and §7. Walls stop, barricades redirect, turrets kill.

road.name: Groundwork
road._doc: §4b. Roads, slabs and paving — these paint terrain as well as geometry.

structures.name: Banner
structures.desc: A long hanging of dyed cloth. Says somebody lives here.

structures.name: Brazier
structures.desc: An iron bowl of coals on three legs. Warm, loud, and visible from the treeline.

structures.name: Bench
structures.desc: Two trestles and a board. Somewhere to sit and look at what you have made.

structures.name: Table and Chairs
structures.desc: A plank table with four stools. Where a camp becomes a household.

structures.name: Rug
structures.desc: Woven, worn, and the wrong colour for the room. Perfect.

structures.name: Bookshelf
structures.desc: Ledgers, star tables and one novel somebody left behind.

structures.name: Crate and Barrel Stack
structures.desc: Empty, mostly. A yard without clutter looks abandoned.

structures.name: Hanging Sign
structures.desc: A painted board on a bracket. Squeaks in a wind.

structures.name: Statue
structures.desc: Somebody standing on a plinth, weathered past recognising.

structures.name: Fountain
structures.desc: A basin, a spout and the sound of moving water. The most civilised thing you can build.

structures.name: Planter
structures.desc: A trough of earth with something green in it.

structures.name: Flower Bed
structures.desc: Edged in stone, planted with whatever survives here.

structures.name: Hedge
structures.desc: A run of clipped shrub. Stops nothing, divides everything.

structures.name: Fence
structures.desc: Post and rail. For keeping animals in, not raiders out.

structures.name: Fence Gate
structures.desc: A gap in the fence with a latch on it.

structures.name: Lamp Post
structures.desc: An oil lamp on a cast post. The first thing to build after the walls.

structures.name: Wall Sconce
structures.desc: A bracket and a flame, close enough to a doorway to find the door.

structures.name: Hanging Lantern
structures.desc: Glass and iron on a chain. Swings, and the shadows swing with it.

structures.name: Crystal Lamp
structures.desc: A cut crystal on a steel stem, lit from inside. Cold, steady, and reaches twice as far as a flame.

structures.name: Window Box
structures.desc: Flowers under a window. Nobody needs it, which is why it matters.

structures.name: Shutters
structures.desc: Painted boards either side of a window, hinged to close on a storm.

structures.name: Weather Vane
structures.desc: An iron creature on a spindle, pointing at the weather.

structures.name: Chimney Pot
structures.desc: Fired clay on a stack, smoking gently.

structures.name: Trophy Mount
structures.desc: A skull on a board. Everyone who visits asks about it.

structures.name: Bed
structures.desc: Frame, tick and blanket. Farhold has nights; this is where you spend them.

structures.name: Chest of Drawers
structures.desc: Four drawers, two of which stick.

structures.name: Wardrobe
structures.desc: Tall, dark, and far too heavy to have carried here.

structures.name: Cooking Pot
structures.desc: A black pot on a tripod over embers.

structures.name: Washing Line
structures.desc: Two poles and a rope of shirts. The single fastest way to make a place look lived in.

structures.name: Well Head
structures.desc: A ring of stone, a windlass and a bucket.

structures.name: Dovecote
structures.desc: A tower of nesting holes. The birds arrive on their own.

structures.name: Beehive
structures.desc: A stack of straw skeps. Loud in summer.

structures.name: Scarecrow
structures.desc: Sacking, straw and a hat. It does not fool the crows and it unsettles visitors.

structures.name: Paving Tile
structures.desc: A flagged square. Lays flat because it flattens what is under it.

structures.name: Carpet of Moss
structures.desc: Encouraged rather than planted. Soft underfoot, and quiet.

structures.name: Potted Tree
structures.desc: A sapling in a tub, taken from the treeline and kept.

structures.name: Wind Chime
structures.desc: Hollow copper tubes. You will hear the weather change before you see it.

structures.name: Nameplate
structures.desc: Your name over the door, cut into a board.

structures.name: Crafting Table
structures.desc: The first bench. Tools, basic gear and structure kits.

structures.name: Anvil
structures.desc: Weapons and armour from ingots. Feeds the crafting screen you already have.

structures.name: Workbench
structures.desc: Machine parts, furniture and every decorative piece in this catalogue.

structures.name: Enchanting Altar
structures.desc: Where an affix is talked on to a blade. Hums when nobody is near it.

structures.name: Alchemy Bench
structures.desc: Potions, oils and the explosives you will regret storing indoors.

structures.name: Fletching Bench
structures.desc: Shafts, heads and fletches. Quivers do not fill themselves.

structures.name: Cooking Station
structures.desc: A hearth, a griddle and a rack. Food buffs come from here.

structures.name: Campfire
structures.desc: Tier nought. Cook, boil, burn. Free, and no power.

structures.name: Furnace
structures.desc: Ore in, ingot out, coal or wood underneath. The first real structure.

structures.name: Kiln
structures.desc: Clay to brick, sand to glass. Takes a day to cool.

structures.name: Smelter
structures.desc: A faster furnace that takes several ores at once — and takes power to do it.

structures.name: Alloy Forge
structures.desc: Two ingots in, one better one out. This is the gate on mid-tier gear.

structures.name: Sawmill
structures.desc: Logs to planks and beams at a rate that does not insult you.

structures.name: Stonecutter
structures.desc: Rubble to cut block. The wall tool eats its output.

structures.name: Tannery
structures.desc: Hides to leather. Build it downwind.

structures.name: Loom
structures.desc: Fibre to cloth, cloth to rope, rope to everything.

structures.name: Chemical Bench
structures.desc: Sulphur, salt and water into reagents.

structures.name: Refinery
structures.desc: Reagents and ore into refined compounds. The tier-two gate, and loud about it.

structures.name: Crusher
structures.desc: Ore to dust. More metal per rock, at the cost of the grid.

structures.name: Washer
structures.desc: Dust and water to concentrate. One more step, one more yield.

structures.name: Assembler
structures.desc: Components into machine parts. Nothing at tier three exists without it.

structures.name: Crystal Cutter
structures.desc: Raw crystal into lenses and focusers. Everything that aims light starts here.

structures.name: Fuel Synthesiser
structures.desc: The last structure before the sky opens. Every flight burns what comes out of it.

structures.name: Drill
structures.desc: Stands on an ore node and works it without you. Hand-mining is slow so that this feels like a promotion.

structures.name: Pump
structures.desc: Water out of a river, a lake or a well, into the pool.

structures.name: Hauler Post
structures.desc: A drone and a perch for it. Carries between two pools that do not reach each other.

structures.name: Storage Crate
structures.desc: Twenty slots. Anything in reach of a logistics pole is in reach of the whole base.

structures.name: Storage Silo
structures.desc: Bulk. Stone, ore and grain, and the reason the pool idea beats belts.

structures.name: Logistics Pole
structures.desc: Draws the pool's edge on the ground. Stores inside it share everything.

structures.name: Burner Generator
structures.desc: Coal in, power out, smoke everywhere. Duty-cycles down when the grid is idle.

structures.name: Wind Turbine
structures.desc: Free power when the weather agrees, which on some worlds is never.

structures.name: Solar Array
structures.desc: Nothing at night — which is what makes a battery bank a real decision.

structures.name: Geothermal Tap
structures.desc: Sunk into a vent. Steady day and night, and only some worlds have one.

structures.name: Battery Bank
structures.desc: Carries the night for the solar array, and the gap between waves for the turrets.

structures.name: Power Pole
structures.desc: Carries the grid. You should be able to see what is connected, and this is how.

structures.name: Palisade
structures.desc: Sharpened stakes in a ditch. Tier one of three, and better than nothing by a long way.

structures.name: Stone Wall
structures.desc: Cut block, coursed. Stops most things that walk.

structures.name: Reinforced Wall
structures.desc: Block with a steel spine. Stops the things that do not walk.

structures.name: Gate
structures.desc: Opens for you, and not for them. Put it where your road crosses your wall.

structures.name: Watchtower
structures.desc: Line of sight, and somewhere a hired archer can actually stand.

structures.name: Arrow Turret
structures.desc: Cheap, fast, and individually unimpressive. Build six.

structures.name: Ballista Turret
structures.desc: Slow, heavy, one target at a time. What you point at the big one.

structures.name: Flame Turret
structures.desc: Short reach, wide cone, superb against a pack and useless against one big thing.

structures.name: Frost Turret
structures.desc: Barely scratches anything. Slows everything — the only crowd control you get.

structures.name: Arc Coil
structures.desc: Jumps from one to the next. Expensive, and it will take your grid down if you build two.

structures.name: Spike Trap
structures.desc: Area denial for the price of a fence panel.

structures.name: Caltrops
structures.desc: Scattered iron. Slows a charge to a walk.

structures.name: Pit Trap
structures.desc: The terrain tool and a cover over it. Digs itself when you place it.

structures.name: Barricade
structures.desc: Does not stop them; sends them the long way round. The primitive the whole defence rests on.

structures.name: Repair Station
structures.desc: Patches structures between waves so you can watch the fight instead of the hammer.

structures.name: Alarm Bell
structures.desc: Early warning — and ring it yourself to start the wave on your terms, for a better purse.

structures.name: Guard Post
structures.desc: A brazier, a roof and two stools. Spend gold instead of materials and somebody stands here.

structures.name: Shield Pylon
structures.desc: Eats a fixed amount of damage per wave and then goes dark. Buys you a minute, which is usually enough.

structures.name: Ammo Hopper
structures.desc: Turrets need feeding. This is where the logistics pool stops being an abstraction.

structures.name: Foundation Slab
structures.desc: Flatten and floor in one action. Everything else stands on these.

structures.name: Dirt Track
structures.desc: Painted, not placed. Flattens under itself and joins the world's own road graph.

structures.name: Gravel Road
structures.desc: Drains, and does not turn to soup in the rain.

structures.name: Cobbled Road
structures.desc: Set stone with a kerb. Traffic from the real road will use it.

structures.name: Outpost Marker
structures.desc: Optional. Names the outpost it stands in and marks its middle, which is where a raid comes. Round 14: it does not permit anything — you can build anywhere without one.

structures.name: Waypoint Pad
structures.desc: The same round concrete pad and the same sigil ring as every other waypoint in the network — because it IS the network. Needs a seated core and a live grid, or the sigils go dark and nobody can travel to it.

_defenceDoc: A `defence` block is what makes a defensive structure SHOOT: range in metres, damage a hit, `every` seconds between shots, `splash` metres of area, and an element that js/effects.js already understands. A wall, a gate, a trap or a barricade has no block and does not fire — the category alone is not enough, because js/defence.js gates on the block rather than on `cat` and a palisade must never snipe. Tuned here so the numbers live beside the costs they are paid for.
